subject: Post-call: embedding spec handoff & next steps for ACME Retail
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmeretail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: embedding spec handoff & next steps for ACME Retail

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the 30-minute call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Goal: Replace current vendor's embedding pipeline to reduce per-query cost by ~40% and improve similarity recall for product descriptions + short reviews.
- Data: ~8M product descriptions, 120M review snippets; new embeddings run as offline batch with incremental daily updates (~150k new vectors/day).
- Current provider: vendorX (floating-dim, L2 norms applied client-side).
- Constraints: must support per-tenant routing and PII scrubbed before vectorization.

Key technical considerations we flagged
1) Vector dimensionality: you prefer 768 for catalog + 256 for short snippets to save cost.
2) Normalization: vendorX stored unnormalized vectors; ACME currently normalizes on retrieval. We recommended storing normalized vectors (unit-length) to simplify cosine/similarity math.
3) Batching: initial ingest will be large — want best throughput while keeping Redis-based ANN index warm during migration.
4) Auth & SDK: require SSO-friendly API keys and a simple Node + Python SDK snippet for bulk uploads.
5) Reranker: interested in a lightweight reranker using a small cross-encoder for top-100 re-score.

Proposed next steps
- Action 1 (this week): Send a short embedding spec (vector dims, dtype, normalization policy, sample CSV) — Marissa to attach a sample CSV + proposal.
- Action 2 (by Tue): Technical deep-dive w/ ACME infra (1h) to confirm network egress, KMS, and VPC options — Aditya to lead.
- Action 3 (by next Fri): Pilot plan + cost estimate for a 100k-vector pilot and migration runbook.

I'll attach our draft proposal and a sample embeddings CSV for your team to validate. Please reply with any immediate blockers and confirm availability for the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Diego
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_embed_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal, 3pp), acme_sample_embeddings.csv (first 500 rows)

Subject: Re: Post-call: embedding spec handoff & next steps for ACME Retail

Priya / Liam —

Dropping the embedding spec and a minimal SDK example below. Diego attached the proposal + CSV in his note; I'm including the spec fields we typically validate during pilots. If anything here looks off, mark it and we'll adjust.

Embedding spec (recommended defaults)
- Namespace: acme_catalog_v1
- Vector dims: 768 for products, 256 for review_snippets
- DType: float32 (we support float16 for cost optimization; see notes)
- Normalization: store vectors as unit-length (L2 normalize at encode time)
- ID format: stable UUID v4 for each item; include source_timestamp and version tag
- Batching: 8k-32k vectors per upload chunk depending on instance size (we'll probe throughput)
- Upserts: support versioned upserts (overwrite if version > stored_version)
- ANN index warm strategy: rolling pre-warm + small initial shard allocation for pilot

Quick SDK snippets
- Node (bulk upload, simplified):

const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
await client.embeddings.upsertBatch('acme_catalog_v1', batchVectors);

- Python (generator upload):

from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
client.embeddings.upsert_batch('acme_catalog_v1', generator_of_vectors)

Auth & routing notes
- We support API keys tied to HubSpot account and can map keys to tenant routing policy. For SSO we can integrate with your IdP and provision scoped keys.
- For private deployments, we’ll use a customer-managed VPC peering with egress rules for the collector.

Reranker suggestion
- Use a 3-step flow: retrieve top-1k with ANN, rerank top-100 with a small cross-encoder (fine-tuned on ACME QA pairs), then return top-10. Cost-friendly and empirically better for relevance.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear spec. A few quick clarifying Qs from our infra/ML teams: 

1) Why recommend storing normalized vectors versus normalizing at query time? VendorX currently stores unnormalized vectors and normalizes at query. Will storing normalized vectors limit us if we change similarity metric later?
2) For batching you list 8k-32k — what hardware assumptions are those numbers based on? We run on GCP a2-highgpu-1 now for training and want to know expected throughput for uploads.
3) Re: dtype float32 vs float16 — what's the retrieval quality delta you've observed for dense product descriptions?

Also — can you provide the exact expected CSV schema (column names/sample row) so our export script team can map fields?

If we can get that before Tue we'll be ready for the deep-dive.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call: embedding spec handoff & next steps for ACME Retail

Hi Liam / Priya —

Good questions — answering inline.

1) Normalized storage tradeoffs
- Recommendation: store vectors normalized (unit L2) at encode time. Rationale: cosine similarity becomes a simple dot product which reduces compute at query time and avoids repeated normalization costs for high-QPS retrieval. If you later want to use a different metric (e.g., L2) you can still store the pre-normalized float vector and also keep the pre-normalized copy in archive (we support storing both). Practically, most similarity use-cases for product catalog + snippet recall use cosine and benefit from normalized store.

2) Batching assumptions and throughput guidance
- Numbers (8k–32k) assume a modern g4dn/g5 or a2-type instance with network egress ~10 Gbps and Redwood Dedicated worker pool sized for medium batch IO. Pilot run: we recommend probing at 8k to validate latency and increase to 32k if throughput is stable.
- Example: on an a2-highgpu-1 instance we measured ~45k vectors/minute for 768-d float32 batches at 16k chunk size (with our optimized batching pipeline). We'll include probe scripts in the deep-dive.

3) float32 vs float16 quality
- Float16 reduces memory and bandwidth by ~2x. For product descriptions we typically see negligible retrieval quality loss for cosine if embeddings are produced with well-conditioned models — but small numeric noise can impact very tight nearest neighbors. Recommendation: pilot with float16 for the short-snippet index and float32 for the product catalog. We'll surface A/B metrics during the pilot.

CSV schema (sample row)
- id, source_timestamp, version, title, description, category, vector_0 ... vector_767 (for 768-d)
- Example (tab-delimited):
123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000	2026-11-17T08:12:00Z	3	"Classic Leather Wallet"	"Full-grain leather wallet, 6 slots"	"Accessories"	0.0032	-0.2101	...

We'll attach a simple conversion script and a probe script to the Drive folder for your export team.

Next steps:
- Diego: confirm Tue deep-dive time (Aditya & Sofia to lead technical session).
- Marissa: I'll follow up with the probe scripts and a short note about float16 testing.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
